key_facts: VN.ai, a startup that stress tests generative AI for copyright infringement, produced its first quarterly report on 15 AI models
Midjourney v8.1 was the worst offender at reproducing images of copyrighted characters
It also led on brand-safety violations: such characters in harmful contexts in 37% of prompts, about one in three
Every model generated at least one protected character, including Google's Nano Banana and ByteDance's Seedance 2.5
Disney and NBCUniversal sued Midjourney last year; Warner Bros Discovery also sued; the suits continue
Midjourney did not respond; it has argued training on copyrighted images is fair use
quote_evidence: The research conducted last month found that Midjourney v8.1 was the worst offender when it came to reproducing images of copyrighted characters.
Midjourney did not respond to requests for comment.
why_it_matters_hint: Third-party testing suggests copyright problems persist across image and video models.
notes: Findings come from one startup's tests, shared exclusively with Deadline.
title: Midjourney: Report Claims AI Model Is Worst Offender For Flouting Hollywood Copyright
